fixes.explanation: A soldier's heart isn't what Pharaoh names, friend. Joseph had just explained the dreams and suggested a plan for the food (Genesis 41:25-36), and that's what the king has heard. So Pharaoh asks about someone “…in whom the Spirit of God abides?” That's the answer, and it has nothing to do with armor.

Fine linen, friend. Pharaoh “…clothed him in garments of fine linen…” Joseph walks in with a plan and comes out dressed for the job. Me? I own one outfit, a white apron, and it's had flour on it since day one.

The text says, “…Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt.” Earlier, the writer tells us he was seventeen (Genesis 37:2), so the Bible gives us both ages. I spent a long stretch in a junk drawer, and the only thing anybody handed me was dust. Joseph got a whole land to take charge of.

Fields, yes. The text says, “In every city he laid up the food from the fields around it.” Each city's food came from its own surrounding fields. It's like keeping a cookie jar in every room instead of one jar at the far end of the house.

Hills, I'd have loved that answer, friend. A cookie would roll right down one. But the text puts it this way: “In every city he laid up the food from the fields around it.” Fields are the word in the verse.

Pharaoh doesn't tell them to sit tight. The people cried out for food, and he told all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.” That's a direction with an address on it. If I told a hungry crowd to go home and wait, they'd have my bakery door off its hinges.
